title: Base C300: what this guide establishes
html: This guide concerns the base C300, not the C300 Pro, Pro V2 or S300. Furniblog has not conducted a sitting test. We distinguish published specifications from our editorial buying checks rather than treating marketing claims as measured results.

title: Manufacturer and seller descriptions disagree
html: The linked Amazon model describes 3D armrests, while SIHOO's product page uses 4D. We cannot establish identical delivered hardware from those labels. Ask the seller which movements are available on the selected item.

match: The designer and the design story
title: Use documentation for the correct model
html: During our September 10, 2026 check, the manufacturer page's Download Manual link led to a PDF labelled M18. We did not use that document as a C300 setup or fit reference. Before assembly, match the manual's model identifier to the chair and request the correct document if they differ.

title: Compare the seat, not just the appearance
html: Think about whether you prefer a mesh or padded seat based on chairs you already use. Product photographs cannot establish seat firmness, edge pressure or long-term comfort. Keep those questions separate from the appearance of the frame.

match: Ergonomics & how it supports the body
title: Adaptive support is not a comfort guarantee
html: SIHOO describes adaptive lumbar support. That is a mechanism description, not evidence that the chair will suit every user. If you need a particular support position, obtain the exact adjustment diagram and evaluate the available return terms before ordering.

title: Do not infer a seat slider from a depth range
html: A specification listing multiple seat-depth values does not, on its own, prove that the base chair has adjustable seat travel. We have removed the earlier sliding-seat claim. Ask the seller to identify the relevant control on the exact model instead of borrowing a feature from a Pro review.

title: Check the controls you actually need
html: Before buying, distinguish a recline angle from the available lock positions and resistance controls. If manual tension adjustment or an armrest lock is essential to you, ask the seller to demonstrate it. These are purchase checks, not defects observed in a Furniblog test.

title: What remains untested
html: We have not measured frame rigidity, mesh wear, armrest stability or assembly time. We therefore do not describe the materials as premium or claim that they will remain comfortable through years of use. Keep the order documentation for any warranty claim.

title: Comfort evidence and limits
html: Furniblog has not hands-on tested the C300. Earlier unattributed comfort anecdotes and first-person-sounding evaluations have been removed. No universal comfort, pain-relief or durability outcome is established by this guide.

title: A practical fit check before ordering
html: Record the seat-to-floor height, usable seat depth and arm clearance of a chair that works with your desk. Request the matching dimensions for the selected C300. Do not substitute overall chair height for seat height, or treat a person's height alone as proof of fit.

title: Returns, warranty and ownership checks
html: Check the terms attached to the seller and region you order from. Establish whether an assembled chair is returnable, who pays return shipping, and how warranty parts are supplied. A trial or warranty advertised by a different store is not automatically part of your order.
